tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Eclipse Cargo Tracker is a Jakarta EE showcase of Domain-Driven Design for tracking shipping cargo. Start with the README and the license.

tour.title: Build and Deployment Configuration
tour.description: The Maven POM declares the Jakarta EE dependencies; web.xml, beans.xml, faces-config.xml and persistence.xml wire up CDI, JSF and JPA.

tour.title: Domain Core: Aggregates
tour.description: The heart of DDD: the Cargo aggregate with its Itinerary, RouteSpecification and Delivery value objects, identified by TrackingId.

tour.title: Handling Events, Locations and Voyages
tour.description: Handling events record what happens to cargo; Location and Voyage model the shipping network. Repositories are interfaces defined in the domain.

tour.title: Shared Domain Utilities
tour.description: The Specification pattern building blocks (And/Or/Not) used for domain rules.

tour.title: Application Services
tour.description: Transactional use-case services orchestrate the domain: booking, handling events and cargo inspection.

tour.title: Persistence Infrastructure
tour.description: JPA repositories implement the domain repository interfaces.

tour.title: Messaging and Events
tour.description: JMS consumers and CDI events decouple handling registration from cargo inspection and notifications.

tour.title: Pathfinder Routing
tour.description: A separate pathfinder module exposes a REST graph traversal service; ExternalRoutingService is the anti-corruption layer calling it.

tour.title: Booking UI and Facade
tour.description: JSF backing beans use a facade and DTO assemblers to shield the UI from the domain model; XHTML pages and the Faces flow render it.

tour.title: Tracking and Real-time Updates
tour.description: Public tracking page plus WebSocket-based real-time cargo updates.

tour.title: Handling Report Entry Points
tour.description: Handling events enter via REST, file batch jobs and the mobile event logger.

tour.title: Tests and Sample Data
tour.description: Unit tests, an end-to-end lifecycle scenario and sample data show expected behaviour.
